page: Microsoft Azure DC2ds_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the DDCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1D cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB per core, and includes a 154 GB local disk with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The single-core Geekbench score of 1664.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1897.09 fall into the average tier. However, multi-core performance is limited, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3005.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 19.64 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 26.16 GB/sec for large-block read operations. For lightweight workloads, it demonstrates average performance in text processing and small-model LLM inference, achieving 122.46 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC2ds_v3 provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 at a low entry-level resource tier, making it a viable option for memory-sensitive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. Given the 2-core limitation and weaker multi-core benchmarks, this instance is best suited for lightweight databases, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, or development environments requiring dedicated CPU allocation and local storage.
